overview.summary: This chapter explores the development of historiography in the Western world, covering key thinkers and their contributions to historical writing. It introduces various schools of thought including dialectics, Marxist, Subaltern, and Feminist historiography.
youWillLearn: Identify the founders and key contributors to modern historiography.
Understand different schools of historical thought.
Explain the contributions of Georg Hegel, Karl Marx, Leopold von Ranke, and Simone de Beauvoir.
Recognize the different types of historiography like Subaltern and Feminist.
Understand the concept of dialectics and class struggle.

notes.title: Introduction to Historiography
notes.content: Historiography is the study of the methods and principles of historical writing. It examines how history is written and the various perspectives that influence it.

notes.title: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
notes.content: Hegel was a German philosopher known for his concept of dialectics. He wrote 'Reason in History'. He believed that history is a rational process and that the development of human consciousness is driven by dialectical reasoning.

notes.title: Karl Marx
notes.content: Karl Marx was a philosopher and historian who focused on class struggle. He believed that history is driven by economic factors and conflicts between different social classes. He wrote 'The Communist Manifesto' and 'Das Kapital'.

notes.title: Leopold von Ranke
notes.content: Ranke is considered the father of modern historiography. He emphasized the importance of examining historical documents minutely. His famous work is 'The Theory and Practice of History'. He believed history should be written as it actually happened.

notes.title: Simone de Beauvoir
notes.content: Simone de Beauvoir was a French feminist scholar who insisted on rethinking the male-dominated perspective in historiography. She argued for including women's perspectives in historical writing, giving rise to feminist historiography.

notes.title: Voltaire - Founder of Modern Historiography
notes.content: It may be said that Voltaire was the founder of modern historiography. He emphasized writing history from a critical and rational perspective.

notes.title: Important Thinkers and Their Works
rows: The Theory and Practice of History

right: The Theory and Practice of History

notes.title: Feminist Historiography
notes.question: What is feminist historiography?
notes.qnaAnswer: Feminist historiography means writing history with a women's perspective. It emerged as a reaction to the dominance of male perspective in historical writing. Simone de Beauvoir insisted on including women's perspectives, making various aspects of women's lives like employment, trade union roles, and family life part of historiography.

notes.title: Karl Marx's View on History
notes.question: Explain Karl Marx's perspective on history.
notes.qnaAnswer: Karl Marx believed that history was not about abstract ideas but about the fundamental needs of people. He argued that the means of production and class struggle are the driving forces of history. According to him, history is the history of class struggles, where one class exploits the rest of society.

overview.summary: This chapter examines the Indian tradition of historiography, focusing on historians who wrote about India's past. It covers the works of Indian and British historians who documented Indian history.
youWillLearn: Identify key Indian historians and their works.
Understand the contributions of British historians to Indian historiography.
Recognize the importance of different historical sources.
Appreciate the diverse perspectives in Indian historical writing.

notes.title: Indian Historiography
notes.content: Indian historiography includes works by both Indian and British historians. Notable Indian historians include V.D. Savarkar, Damodar Kosambi, Ramchandra Guha, and Sharmila Rege, each representing different schools of thought.

notes.title: Nationalistic Historiography
notes.content: Nationalistic historiography focuses on India's struggle for independence and the nation's history from a nationalist perspective. V.D. Savarkar is associated with this school of thought.

notes.title: Marxist Historiography
notes.content: Marxist historiography applies Marxist principles to analyze Indian history, focusing on class struggles and economic factors. Damodar Kosambi was a notable exponent of this approach.

notes.title: Subaltern Historiography
notes.content: Subaltern historiography focuses on the history of the oppressed and marginalized groups, giving voice to those who are often excluded from mainstream historical narratives. Ranjit Guha is a key figure in this school, and similar thoughts were expressed by Mahatma Phule and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.

notes.title: Feminist Historiography
notes.content: Feminist historiography in the Indian context focuses on women's contributions and perspectives. Sharmila Rege is associated with this approach, which seeks to correct male-dominated historical narratives.

quiz.explanation: V.D. Savarkar is known for his nationalistic approach to Indian history.

quiz.explanation: Subaltern historiography gives voice to oppressed and marginalized communities.

overview.summary: This chapter explores the practical application of historical knowledge in fields like heritage management, tourism, and conservation. It discusses the importance of preserving and conserving historical artifacts and sites for future generations.
youWillLearn: Understand the concept of applied history.
Explain the importance of archives and museums.
Identify methods of preserving and conserving heritage.
Recognize the role of UNESCO in heritage management.
Understand the need for trained professionals in conservation.

notes.title: Applied History
notes.content: Applied history refers to the practical use of historical knowledge in various fields such as heritage management, tourism, archival science, and museum studies. It involves preserving, conserving, and presenting historical artifacts and sites.

notes.title: Archives
notes.content: A place where historical documents are preserved is called an 'Archive'. Many old documents, official records, films, and records of treaties are kept here. The National Archives of India in Delhi is the largest archive in Asia. Every state in India maintains its archives independently.

notes.title: Why Archives are Important
notes.content: Archives provide references to original documents, allowing for the study of historical events of a particular period. They help us understand the language and script used in a particular era, making them invaluable for historical research.

notes.title: Vishwakosh (Encyclopaedia)
notes.content: A comprehensive encyclopaedia (Vishwakosh) contains information on all known subjects. It is an important medium for documenting and disseminating information. Two types exist: one covering all subjects (e.g., Encyclopaedia Britannica), and another focused on a single subject (e.g., Bharatiya Samskruti Kosh).

notes.title: Conservation and Preservation
notes.content: Only trained and qualified persons can undertake conservation and preservation tasks. The skill required for each task is different, and the procedures and precautions involved are specific. This ensures that historical artifacts and sites are protected for future generations.

notes.title: Why Only Trained Persons Can Handle Conservation?
notes.question: Only trained persons who are duly qualified can take up the tasks involved in the work of conservation and preservation.
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) Historical research and conservation involve different tasks like collecting, preserving, and exhibiting sources. 2) The skill required for each task is different, and the procedure and precautions to be taken are also specific. 3) To ensure that artifacts and sites are protected correctly, only trained and qualified professionals should handle these responsibilities.

This chapter explores the relationship between mass media and history, discussing how newspapers, radio, and television have evolved and influenced society. It covers the role of media in democracy and its importance as a historical source.
youWillLearn: Identify the pioneers of print media in India.
Understand the history of radio and television in India.
Recognize newspapers as an important educational and informational medium.
Explain the role of media as the 'fourth pillar of democracy'.
Identify key figures in the development of Indian media.

notes.title: Development of Newspapers in India
notes.content: The first English newspaper in India was started by James Augustus Hickey. 'Darpan' was the first newspaper in Marathi. 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' were started by Agarkar and Tilak. Newspapers are known as the 'fourth pillar of democracy'.

notes.title: Radio in India
notes.content: The Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) was the first to broadcast daily programmes. It was later taken over and renamed the Indian State Broadcasting Service (ISBS), and on 8th June 1936, it was renamed 'All India Radio (AIR)'. The famous poet Pandit Narendra Sharma suggested the name 'Akashvani'. Its motto is 'Bahujanhiary Bahujansukhay'.

notes.title: Television in India
notes.content: Television is an audio-visual medium. The first English news bulletin was broadcast on 23rd July 1927 from the Mumbai radio station. Television serves as both an educational and entertainment medium.

notes.title: Importance of Newspapers
notes.content: Newspapers report events that are interesting to the public but also cover important issues like war, global warming, education, and national elections. They have contributed significantly to literacy and the spread of democratic freedoms. They help shape opinions in the global village.

notes.title: Balshastri Jambhekar
notes.content: Balshastri Jambhekar started 'Digdarshan', the first monthly magazine in Marathi. He was a pioneer in Marathi journalism.

notes.title: 'Shatpatre' Letters
notes.content: The letters 'Shatpatre' published in Prabhakar were written by Lokhitvadi (Gopal Hari Deshmukh). These letters were influential in shaping social reform in Maharashtra.

notes.title: Why is Newspaper an Important Medium of Education and Information?
notes.question: Newspaper is an important medium of education and information.
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) Newspapers report interesting events and also cover important issues like war, global warming, education, and national elections. 2) They have contributed to the spread of literacy and the concept of human rights and democratic freedoms. 3) They are integral to the development of democracy and help shape public opinion.

notes.title: Akashvani Programmes
notes.question: Which programmes are broadcast by Akashvani?
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) Initially, Akashvani broadcasted government programmes and schemes. 2) It later broadcasted various entertainment and literary programmes. 3) It presents programmes for creating awareness. 4) Special programmes are also broadcasted for farmers, workers, youth and women.

This chapter examines the historical development of sports in India and the world. It covers traditional Indian games, modern sports, and the cultural and historical significance of sports and toys.
youWillLearn: Identify the origins of the Olympic Games.
Recognize traditional Indian sports and games.
Understand the cultural significance of toys in history.
Identify key Indian sports personalities and their achievements.
Trace the development of toys and their importance in cultural history.

notes.title: Origins of the Olympic Games
notes.content: The ancient Olympic competitions used to be held at Olympia in Greece. These games had great historical and cultural significance in the ancient world.

notes.title: National Game of India
notes.content: Hockey is the national game of India. The National Sports Day is celebrated on 29th August, the birth date of Major Dhyan Chand, who was honored with Padma Bhushan for his achievements in hockey.

notes.title: Traditional Indian Sports
notes.content: Traditional Indian sports include Mallakhamb (outdoor game based on physical skills), Water Polo (water sport), Skating (adventure ice sport), and Chess (indoor game). Wooden dolls made in Maharashtra are known as 'Thaki'. Other traditional games include Langadi, Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Marbles, Lagori, Vitti-Dandu, Bhingari, Phugadi, and Zimma.

notes.title: Toys and Cultural History
notes.content: A tradition of making different types of toys for entertainment exists since ancient times. Toys give us an idea about cultural and religious development of that period. Clay models of forts and images of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj are made during Diwali in Maharashtra. An ivory doll found at Pompeii sheds light on Indo-Roman trade. Games and toys are mentioned in Kathasaritsagara.

notes.title: Key Sports Personalities
notes.content: Major Dhyan Chand was honored with Padma Bhushan. Sachin Tendulkar was honored with Bharat Ratna. Mary Kom was the first Indian female boxer to win a bronze medal in the Olympics. Khashaba Jadhav was also a notable Indian Olympic medalist.

notes.title: Mirchchhakatika and Kathasaritsagara
notes.content: Shudraka wrote the play 'Mirchchhakatika' which means 'a clay cart'. An interesting description of games and toys is found in Kathasaritsagara.

notes.title: How Toys Tell Us About Cultural History
notes.question: How can toys tell us about cultural history?
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) Toys give us an idea about the cultural and religious development of that period. 2) Clay models of forts and clay images of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj made during Diwali give us an idea about the structures of forts. 3) An ivory doll found at Pompeii sheds light on Indo-Roman trade and cultural relations. 4) The mention of games and toys in Kathasaritsagara gives us an idea about cultural history.

overview.summary: This chapter explores the relationship between tourism and history, discussing different types of tourism and their historical significance. It covers the pioneers of tourism and the various purposes of tourism.
youWillLearn: Identify the pioneers of modern tourism.
Understand the different types of tourism.
Explain the various purposes of tourism.
Recognize the historical significance of travel and tourism.

notes.title: Pioneers of Tourism
notes.content: Thomas Cook established a travel agency selling tourist tickets. In Maharashtra, Gopal Neelkanth Dandekar used to arrange hiking tours to explore sights linked to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The Chinese monk Yuan Shiwang traveled in India in 630 C.E. Hiuen Tsang was another famous Chinese traveler.

notes.title: Bhilar - Village of Books
notes.content: Near Mahabaleshwar, Bhilar is known as the 'Village of Books'. This is a unique initiative promoting tourism through literature and reading.

notes.title: Purposes of Tourism
notes.content: Tourism has various purposes including visiting historical monuments, museums, pilgrim centres, beaches, mountain ranges, national parks, and industrial sites. Sports tourism, cultural tourism, and eco-tourism are popular forms of tourism.

notes.title: Famous Travelers in History
notes.content: Marco Polo, Thomas Cook, Benjamin of Tudela, and Gerardus Mercator were notable travelers who contributed to the development of tourism and exploration.

notes.title: Explain the Purpose of Tourism
notes.question: Explain the purpose of tourism.
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) To see historical monuments, forts, and cities discovered during excavations. 2) To visit pilgrim centres, sea beaches, mountain ranges, valleys, snow-capped peaks, and pristine jungles. 3) To visit special plateaus, museums, and places of natural beauty. 4) To see medicinal plants and avail of ayurvedic therapies. 5) To visit agricultural projects and research centres. 6) To watch sports events (sports tourism) or dance-music festivals (cultural tourism). 7) To attend film festivals, science seminars, international conferences, and literary events.

overview.summary: This chapter focuses on the preservation and management of cultural and natural heritage. It discusses museums, world heritage sites, and the importance of conserving heritage for future generations.

Understand the role of UNESCO in heritage management.
Recognize the importance of preserving cultural heritage.
Identify key figures in heritage conservation.

notes.title: Major Museums
notes.content: The Indian Museum in Kolkata is the first museum in India. The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastusamgrahalay was built to commemorate the visit of the Prince of Wales. The Louvre Museum in Paris houses the famous painting 'Mona Lisa' by Leonardo da Vinci.

notes.title: UNESCO and World Heritage
notes.content: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) has given directives to preserve and conserve cultural and natural heritage for future generations. The Kas Plateau in Maharashtra is listed as a World Natural Heritage Site.

notes.title: Famous Artists
notes.content: Leonardo da Vinci was the 16th-century artist who worked under the patronage of French King Francis I. His famous painting 'Mona Lisa' is housed in the Louvre Museum.

notes.title: Indian Museums
notes.content: The Government Museum, National Museum, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastusamgrahalay are important museums in India. The Museum of Natural History in Switzerland houses more than 12 rare specimens of fossils.

notes.title: Important Encyclopaedias
notes.content: Important encyclopaedias include: Sangeetshastrakar va Kalavant Yancha Ithas (Lakshman Dattatray Joshi), Krantikarakantha Charitrakosh (S.R. Date), Svatantryasainik Charitrakosh (N.R. Phatak), and Bharatvarshiya Prachin Aitihasik Kosh (Raghunath Bhaskar Godbole).

notes.title: Ellora Caves - World Heritage Site
notes.question: Write information about the Ellora Caves.
notes.qnaAnswer: 1) The picture is of the largest Indian rock-cut Hindu temple located in the Ellora cave. 2) This famous rock-cut Shiva temple was constructed during the reign of Rashtrakuta king Krishna I. 3) It is regarded as a world heritage site by UNESCO in 1983. 4) It bears testimony to the high-level skill attained by India in the art of sculpture and architecture.
